title: Duck Duck Grey Duck
about: A spontaneous late-night game that turned into one of the funniest memories from State Arts-In.
description: This track tells the story of an impromptu game of Duck Duck Grey Duck played in the middle of the road during State Arts-In. What started as harmless fun grew as strangers joined in, ending only when the police arrived. The real punchline came afterward when Christoph nervously told my mom what happened, expecting a lecture, only to hear her calmly reply, "Thank you." It's a lighthearted memory about friendship, youthful spontaneity, and the stories that become legends years later.
lyrics: Somewhere in the middle of the road,
Not beside it, not behind it,
Right where traffic ought to stay.
We made a circle under streetlights,
Duck, duck, duck, then grey duck,
And somebody tore across the ground.
Then the police lights came through.
Everybody learned the game could end
Before the final grey duck flew.
The fair had sent the evening crowd
A few drunk strangers saw the game
And thought it looked just right.
Like they'd known us all for years.
Soon the road was full of runners,
Then the police lights came through.
Everybody learned the game could end
Before the final grey duck flew.
An officer made it very clear
The road was not our floor.
The strangers got a louder warning,
And the game was played no more.
But it might have been our best.
Not from police or from the game.
He was sure my mother would be furious
And hold him most to blame.
He had gotten someone's son involved
For a lecture and a mess.
He told her what had happened,
She listened with a straight face,
Needs a moral at the end.
The road is just a road again.
The strangers left the fair that day.
Still I hear that final cue.
